research.topic: rendering-viewer: native iOS 18 rendering stack for the Mapper scan viewer/editor and live LiDAR scan overlay (SceneKit vs RealityKit vs Metal)

facts.claim: SceneKit is deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK: every SceneKit page (framework, SCNView, SCNGeometry, SCNGeometrySource, SCNGeometryElement, SCNHitTestResult, SCNProgram, SCNTechnique, SCNFillMode, SceneView (SwiftUI)) shows introducedAt iOS 8.0 / deprecatedAt iOS 26.0. Framework deprecation note: 'SceneKit is deprecated, use RealityKit instead. For more information, see WWDC25 session 288'. WWDC25 288 transcript: 'This is a soft deprecation, meaning that existing applications that use SceneKit will continue to work', 'SceneKit is now entering maintenance mode. Apple will only fix critical bugs', 'if you're planning a new app or a significant update, SceneKit is not recommended.' It still compiles (deprecation warnings only).
facts.api: class SCNView (scenekit/scnview), @MainActor @preconcurrency struct SceneView, class SCNGeometry ...
facts.availability: iOS 8.0+, deprecated iOS 26.0 (soft; still compiles with warnings on the iOS 26 SDK)
facts.notes: Architecture consequence: do not build a new viewer on SceneKit/ARSCNView. ARSCNView is deprecated too (arkit/arscnview: iOS 11.0, deprecated 26.0, 'Use RealityKit instead').

facts.claim: ARView (RealityKit, UIKit view) is NOT deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK (platforms: iOS 13.0, no deprecatedAt). It supports .ar and .nonAR camera modes, 2D->3D helpers and a collision hit test that returns per-triangle info on iOS 18.
facts.notes: RealityView on iOS (below) has NO project/unproject/ray/hitTest and no attachments; that is the main reason to host the viewer in ARView(.nonAR) via UIViewRepresentable. Note: the older convenience init(frame:cameraMode:) is deprecated; use the 3-argument init.

facts.claim: RealityView (SwiftUI) exists on iOS 18.0 with a virtual camera and built-in gesture camera controls, but only ONE control mode at a time and no projection/raycast helpers on iOS.
facts.availability: RealityView iOS 18.0+; RealityViewCameraContent, RealityViewCamera, realityViewCameraControls(_:), CameraControls iOS 18.0+; RealityViewAttachments is visionOS-only; RealityViewContent (non-camera) is visionOS-only
facts.notes: CameraControls is not an OptionSet (conforms only to Equatable/Hashable/Sendable), so orbit+pan+pinch-zoom cannot be combined; Apple forum thread 774411 (Feb 2025) asking how to combine them is unanswered. Known bug: changing cameraTarget during an active orbit drag gives a wrong orbit (forum 825543). Doc: 'You can use a drag gesture ... to .tilt, .pan, .orbit, or .dolly a virtual camera.' For a real orbit/pan/zoom viewer you will write your own gesture->camera code anyway, so ARView(.nonAR)+PerspectiveCamera is the simpler host.

facts.claim: LowLevelMesh (iOS 18) lets you hand RealityKit your own interleaved vertex buffers (Metal vertex formats), update them in place on CPU or GPU, split a mesh into parts with per-part materialIndex and topology (.triangle or .line), and wrap it in a MeshResource that reflects later edits without regeneration.
facts.notes: Apple's own example vertex: struct MyVertex { var position: SIMD3<Float>; var color: UInt32 } with attributes [.init(semantic: .position, format: .float3, offset: MemoryLayout<Self>.offset(of: \.position)!), .init(semantic: .color, format: .uchar4Normalized_bgra, offset: MemoryLayout<Self>.offset(of: \.color)!)], layout .init(bufferIndex: 0, bufferStride: MemoryLayout<Self>.stride), then mesh.withUnsafeMutableBytes(bufferIndex: 0) { $0.bindMemory(to: MyVertex.self)[i] = ... }, mesh.withUnsafeMutableIndices { $0.bindMemory(to: UInt32.self)... }, mesh.parts.replaceAll([LowLevelMesh.Part(indexCount: 3, topology: .triangle, bounds: BoundingBox(min:max:))]). The doc's 'LowLevelMesh.Descriptor()' no-arg spelling is not in the JSON; use the 5-arg init (all defaulted) to be safe. The doc sample writes 'try MeshResource(from: lowLevelMesh)' but the declaration is async throws: write 'try await MeshResource(from: llm)'. Capacities are fixed at creation (pick an upper bound per chunk).

facts.claim: Face/point picking with exact triangle index exists in RealityKit on iOS 18 via two routes: (a) collision raycast against a static triangle-mesh ShapeResource returns CollisionCastHit.triangleHit (faceIndex, uv); (b) GPU pixelCast returns the primitive index without any CollisionComponent.
facts.availability: generateStaticMesh(positions:faceIndices:) iOS 18.0; generateStaticMesh(from:) iOS 18.0; triangleHit / TriangleHit iOS 18.0; Scene.raycast iOS 13.0; pixelCast / PixelCastHit iOS 18.0; CollisionComponent iOS 13.0
facts.notes: Apple doc for generateStaticMesh(from:): 'Use a low-priority task because generating collision meshes can take a while'; only CollisionComponent mode .default/static and PhysicsBody .static are allowed. generateStaticMesh(positions:faceIndices:) takes UInt16 indices, so chunks must have <= 65,535 vertices if you use that overload (the MeshResource overload has no such limit). Pipeline: point -> arView.ray(through:) -> arView.scene.raycast(origin:direction:length:query:.nearest) -> hit.position / hit.triangleHit?.faceIndex (faceIndex is relative to the hit shape). pixelCast: 'Performs a ray cast against all the geometry in the scene ... ignores entities that lack a ModelComponent with a valid mesh' (no collision shapes needed; async; primitive is the triangle index within meshPart). Measure = simd_distance(hitA.position, hitB.position).

facts.claim: Wireframe rendering is built into RealityKit materials on iOS 18: every built-in material has triangleFillMode = .lines. No SceneKit/Metal needed for wireframe mode.
facts.notes: Also usable for the labeled object boxes: MeshResource.generateBox + UnlitMaterial(color:) with triangleFillMode = .lines gives a wireframe box. Alternative for explicit edges: LowLevelMesh.Part(topology: .line).

facts.claim: No built-in RealityKit material on iOS reads per-vertex colors (MeshDescriptor/MeshBuffers has no color semantic; UnlitMaterial/PBR ignore the LowLevelMesh .color attribute; ShaderGraphMaterial is visionOS-only). Vertex-color display therefore needs CustomMaterial with a Metal surface shader that reads params.geometry().color(). Per-FACE colors (classification, coverage) do NOT need shaders: use one material per color and per-face material indices (MeshDescriptor.materials = .perFace([UInt32]) or LowLevelMesh parts with materialIndex).
facts.availability: CustomMaterial, SurfaceShader, LightingModel iOS 15.0+ (not available on visionOS); MeshDescriptor.Materials iOS 15.0+
facts.notes: Requirements: a .metal file in the target, #include <RealityKit/RealityKit.h>, library = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()!.makeDefaultLibrary()!, and 'Your surface shader must call at least one supported set_*() function or nothing renders'. Lighting model table (PDF): .unlit supports only set_emissive_color(). That geometry().color() picks up a LowLevelMesh .color attribute on iOS is a strong inference (the .color VertexSemantic exists exactly for this and the forum thread confirms it on visionOS via shader graph) but was not seen in an iOS compiled sample: verify with the first CI build (fallback: pack RGB into a uv1 float2/uv0 attribute or use per-face parts). CustomMaterial (Metal source) compiles fine in an unsigned Xcode build; no entitlement involved.

facts.claim: MeshDescriptor + MeshResource.generate is the simpler static path (iOS 15). positions/normals/textureCoordinates come from the MeshBufferContainer protocol; primitives are UInt32 index lists; materials per face. Regenerating via MeshDescriptor runs Apple's mesh optimizer, so it is for load-time only, not per-frame updates.
facts.availability: MeshDescriptor, MeshBuffers, MeshResource.Contents/Model/Part iOS 15.0+; generateBox/generateText iOS 13.0+; generateAsync/replaceAsync are deprecated (use the throwing sync versions)
facts.notes: Apple's MeshDescriptor overview code: var descriptor = MeshDescriptor(name: "triangle"); descriptor.positions = MeshBuffers.Positions([[-1,-1,0],[1,-1,0],[0,1,0]]); descriptor.primitives = .triangles([0,1,2]). The [MeshDescriptor] overload of generate(from:) is 'likely' only because the JSON topic list omits it; every community sample (markhorgan.com, stepinto.vision, maxxfrazer) compiles with 'try MeshResource.generate(from: [descriptor])'. Prefer LowLevelMesh for the big scan chunks and MeshDescriptor only for small static helpers.

facts.claim: Textures: an atlas image becomes a TextureResource (async, from CGImage) and is applied through UnlitMaterial(texture:) (iOS 18) or PhysicallyBasedMaterial.baseColor. Materials expose culling/depth flags needed for a scan viewer (double-sided rendering).
facts.availability: TextureResource(image:withName:options:) iOS 18.0; generate(from:named:options:) async (replacement for deprecated generate(from:withName:options:)); UnlitMaterial(texture:) iOS 18.0; FaceCulling iOS 15.0; ModelComponent iOS 13.0
facts.notes: Use semantic .color for the atlas. Set faceCulling = .none for scan meshes (LiDAR triangles have inconsistent winding). Old TextureResource.generate(from:withName:options:) and generateAsync are deprecated on iOS 26 SDK (still compile).

facts.claim: Scene graph, visibility and label helpers exist for the viewer: hide/show a chunk with Entity.isEnabled; components are set through Entity.components; a BillboardComponent (iOS 18) keeps label meshes facing the camera; PerspectiveCamera entity is the virtual camera for ARView(.nonAR).
facts.availability: Entity/ComponentSet/PerspectiveCamera/AnchorEntity iOS 13.0; PerspectiveCameraComponent defaults iOS 13.0; BillboardComponent iOS 18.0; ModelDebugOptionsComponent iOS 14.0 (no wireframe mode; wireframe is triangleFillMode)
facts.notes: PerspectiveCameraComponent parameter defaults were not printed by the JSON (only the signature); pass all three explicitly. In ARView(.nonAR) you must add a PerspectiveCamera entity to an AnchorEntity(world: .zero) yourself and set arView.environment.background = .color(.black); the orbit camera is your code (yaw/pitch/distance around a target, written to camera.transform each gesture change).

facts.claim: Live LiDAR mesh input (ARKit): ARMeshAnchor exposes vertices/normals/faces as MTLBuffers plus an optional per-face classification buffer; delivered through ARSessionDelegate add/update/remove callbacks when ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification.
facts.notes: Apple's sample reads a face's classification as anchor.geometry.classification![faceIndex] (uchar per face; count == faces.count) and face vertex indices from faces.buffer (Int32 triples, bytesPerIndex 4). Apple's sample sets arView.automaticallyConfigureSession = false and runs its own ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with .meshWithClassification. .showSceneUnderstanding draws Apple's fixed debug colouring (not customizable) so it is only a debugging aid, not the coverage overlay. Copy the anchor buffers immediately: 'the underlying vertex data is owned by the ARMeshAnchor so this geometry becomes invalid when the anchor is updated or removed' (andrewgrant.org).

facts.claim: Community pattern for ARSCNView + per-anchor SCNGeometry (deprecated route, for comparison): SCNGeometrySource(buffer:) wraps the ARGeometrySource MTLBuffer with zero copy, SCNGeometryElement(data:) wraps faces; the whole node geometry must be rebuilt on every renderer(_:didUpdate:for:) and removed in didRemove.
facts.notes: SceneKit has the most convenient built-ins (allowsCameraControl orbit, hitTest with faceIndex, vertex colors via .color semantic with no shader) and is the fastest path to a demo, but it is deprecated and in maintenance mode. Community perf data: single large meshes of 32k-128k triangles render fine at 120 fps on iPad Pro; 750-2,000 separate nodes already make an iPad 10 (iPadOS 18.3) unresponsive (forum 774697, unanswered). Per-face colouring in SceneKit needs either duplicated vertices with a .color source or SCNProgram/shaderModifiers; ~hundreds of chunk nodes is fine, thousands is not.

facts.claim: RealityKit ARView can host the live scan overlay: run your own ARSession/ARWorldTrackingConfiguration on arView.session (automaticallyConfigureSession = false), keep one Entity per ARMeshAnchor (AnchorEntity(anchor:) or manual transform) whose LowLevelMesh you rewrite on each anchor update; coverage colours are per-face parts (4 UnlitMaterials) or a .color vertex attribute + CustomMaterial.

facts.notes: Marked likely because the per-anchor LowLevelMesh rewrite pattern is assembled from verified pieces, not an Apple sample. Throttling: ARKit updates each mesh anchor at most a few times per second and anchors are small (a few thousand triangles), so rebuilding one anchor's buffers per callback is cheap; coalesce anchors into a dirty set and flush at most every 0.25-0.5 s on the main actor, skip anchors outside the camera frustum, and reallocate a LowLevelMesh only when faces.count exceeds its indexCapacity (allocate capacity = 1.5x current). RealityView(.spatialTracking) + SpatialTrackingSession.run(_:session:arConfiguration:) (iOS 18) also lets you own the ARSession, but RealityView lacks project/hitTest so ARView is still the better live host.

facts.claim: Custom Metal renderer (MTKView) is fully available and unrestricted; wireframe is a one-liner; it is the fallback if RealityKit's CustomMaterial/1M-triangle path underperforms, at the cost of writing camera, picking (CPU ray/triangle or GPU id buffer), text labels and texture loading yourself.
facts.availability: MTKView/MTKViewDelegate iOS 9.0+; Metal encoder APIs iOS 8.0+; none deprecated (MTKView gained MTL4 members in iOS 26)
facts.notes: A15 GPU renders 1M triangles with a trivial shader at 60 fps easily; the risk is CPU-side (draw calls, buffer uploads), not GPU. If you keep the chunk vertex struct identical to the LowLevelMesh layout (position float3, normal float3, uv float2, color uchar4), the same buffers can be fed to an MTKView renderer later without changing the data model.

facts.claim: RealityKit performance guidance: Apple gives no numeric triangle budget (DTS engineer, forum 751764: iterate and measure). Older QuickLook guidance was 100k triangles/2048 textures per USDZ, but that is a content guideline, not an engine limit. Creating a new MeshResource from MeshDescriptor each frame is explicitly inefficient (mesh optimizer runs each time); LowLevelMesh exists precisely for frequent updates.
facts.notes: No published benchmark of RealityKit on iPhone at 1M triangles in hundreds of entities was found. Draw-call count (~hundreds of ModelComponents) is within RealityKit's comfort zone; the unknown is CustomMaterial cost over 1M tris on A15 (expect fine for an unlit shader). Plan a frustum/visibility toggle per chunk (isEnabled) and a level-of-detail decimated copy for orbiting if needed.

facts.claim: ARView.Environment.SceneUnderstanding options and .showSceneUnderstanding give occlusion/collision/physics against the LiDAR mesh and a debug visualisation, but no access to per-face colours; they are not a substitute for a custom overlay.

gotchas: SceneKit, SceneView and ARSCNView are all deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK (soft deprecation, maintenance mode). They compile with warnings on Xcode 26.6 and run on iOS 18 and 26, but Apple says 'if you're planning a new app ... SceneKit is not recommended'. Using them only for a throwaway prototype is fine; do not make them the viewer foundation.

RealityView on iOS 18: realityViewCameraControls takes exactly one CameraControls value (struct, not OptionSet), so orbit + two-finger pan + pinch dolly cannot be combined; changing cameraTarget mid-orbit is buggy (forum 825543); there is no project/unproject/ray/hitTest on RealityViewCameraContent and RealityViewAttachments is visionOS-only. ARView(.nonAR) has project(_:), unproject(_:viewport:), ray(through:), hitTest(_:query:mask:) and snapshot; host it in UIViewRepresentable.

No RealityKit built-in material on iOS reads vertex colors. MeshDescriptor has no color buffer at all. For 'vertex colors' mode you need LowLevelMesh with a .color attribute plus a CustomMaterial Metal surface shader (lightingModel .unlit -> set_emissive_color(params.geometry().color().rgb)). Confirm on the first device build that geometry().color() picks up the LowLevelMesh .color attribute; fallback is packing color into uv coordinates or per-face material parts.

CustomMaterial with .unlit lighting model: only set_emissive_color() is honoured; set_base_color() is ignored in unlit. And 'Your surface shader must call at least one supported set_*() function or nothing renders.' CustomMaterial is unavailable on visionOS (irrelevant for iPhone but blocks a future Vision Pro port; ShaderGraphMaterial is the visionOS equivalent).

MeshResource(from: LowLevelMesh) is 'async throws' on iOS 18 even though Apple's overview code omits await; write 'try await'. ShapeResource.generateStaticMesh(from:) is also async and slow ('can take a while'); build collision shapes per chunk in a low-priority Task after the mesh is visible. generateStaticMesh(positions:faceIndices:) is UInt16-indexed (chunks <= 65,535 vertices) while generateStaticMesh(from: MeshResource) has no such limit.

LowLevelMesh capacities (vertexCapacity/indexCapacity) are fixed at creation; over-allocate per chunk/anchor (e.g. 1.5x) and recreate only when exceeded. withUnsafeMutableBytes/withUnsafeMutableIndices are @MainActor; do the CPU-side array building off-main, then copy on main.

ARMeshAnchor buffers are owned by ARKit and are replaced on every update; copy vertices/faces/classification out synchronously inside the delegate callback (or retain the ARMeshGeometry object) before dispatching work. The SceneKit zero-copy SCNGeometrySource(buffer:) trick is exactly what makes ARSCNView samples crash if didUpdate/didRemove are not handled.

ARView.debugOptions .showSceneUnderstanding is a fixed Apple visualisation (not colour-customisable) and Environment.SceneUnderstanding options only affect occlusion/collision/physics; the green/yellow/red/gray coverage overlay must be your own entities. If you also enable .occlusion, your overlay mesh coincides with Apple's occlusion mesh and z-fights; scale the overlay slightly or skip occlusion while scanning.
LiDAR triangles have inconsistent winding: set faceCulling = .none on every scan material (UnlitMaterial/PBR/Custom all expose it) or half the mesh disappears.

Deprecated-but-compiling RealityKit spellings to avoid (they warn on the iOS 26 SDK): ARView(frame:cameraMode:) 2-arg init, MeshResource.generateAsync/replaceAsync, TextureResource.generate(from:withName:options:)/generateAsync/loadAsync, UnlitMaterial.baseColor/tintColor (use .color), ModelDebugOptionsComponent .baseColorTexture.

SceneKit per-node cost: hundreds of chunk nodes are fine, thousands are not (iPad 10 unresponsive at 750-2,000 nodes). RealityKit: keep chunks to the low hundreds of entities and toggle isEnabled by frustum; no official triangle budget exists (Apple DTS: measure and iterate).

Everything required is available at iOS 18.0; nothing here needs iOS 17 compatibility code and nothing needs iOS 26. Set the deployment target to 18.0. If the second phone on iOS 26 shows RealityKit behaviour differences (rendering pipeline was reworked in iOS 26), the ARView-hosted design is unaffected because ARView is not deprecated.
recommendations: Post-scan viewer stack: RealityKit hosted in ARView(frame:cameraMode: .nonAR, automaticallyConfigureSession: false) inside a UIViewRepresentable. One Entity per chunk with a LowLevelMesh (interleaved vertex: position float3, normal float3, uv0 float2, color uchar4Normalized_bgra; uint32 indices) and a ModelComponent whose materials array is swapped per view mode: textured = UnlitMaterial(texture: atlas) (or PhysicallyBasedMaterial.baseColor with tint .white for lit look), solid = UnlitMaterial(color:), wireframe = same material with triangleFillMode = .lines, vertex colors = CustomMaterial(surfaceShader:lightingModel: .unlit) reading params.geometry().color(), classification = LowLevelMesh parts split by class with one UnlitMaterial per class (materialIndex), all with faceCulling = .none. Hide/show chunks with entity.isEnabled. Camera: PerspectiveCamera entity under AnchorEntity(world: .zero) driven by your own orbit/pan/pinch gesture recognizers on the ARView (yaw/pitch/distance around a target point); this avoids RealityView's single-gesture limitation and keeps project(_:) for 2D label overlays.

Picking and measuring: for each chunk build a CollisionComponent from ShapeResource.generateStaticMesh(from: meshResource) in a Task(priority: .low) after display. Tap -> arView.ray(through: point) -> arView.scene.raycast(origin:direction:length: 100, query: .nearest) -> CollisionCastHit.position (+ triangleHit?.faceIndex for face selection; faceIndex is relative to that chunk's shape). Measure = simd_distance(a.position, b.position); draw the segment with a LowLevelMesh Part(topology: .line) or a thin generateBox, label with a SwiftUI overlay positioned via arView.project(midpoint). Alternative without collision shapes: try await scene.pixelCast(from:to:) returning primitive (triangle index) and meshPart; use it for instant picking before collision shapes finish building.

Detected-object boxes: one Entity per object with MeshResource.generateBox(size:cornerRadius: 0) + UnlitMaterial(color:) with triangleFillMode = .lines, plus a child text entity (MeshResource.generateText) with BillboardComponent, or SwiftUI labels placed with arView.project. Keep them in a separate parent Entity so they can be toggled together.

Live scan view: ARView in .ar mode, automaticallyConfigureSession = false, your own ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification (check supportsSceneReconstruction first) and frameSemantics [.sceneDepth] if needed, ARSessionDelegate on arView.session. Per ARMeshAnchor keep an AnchorEntity(anchor:) holding a LowLevelMesh entity; on didAdd/didUpdate copy vertices/normals/classification/faces, compute per-face coverage state, write indices sorted into 4 parts (green/yellow/red/gray materialIndex 0-3) with 4 semi-transparent UnlitMaterials (blending .transparent, faceCulling .none). Coalesce updates in a dirty set flushed at most every 0.25-0.5 s, skip anchors outside the frustum, reallocate only when faces exceed capacity. Do NOT rely on .showSceneUnderstanding except as a debug toggle.

Do not build on SceneKit/ARSCNView (deprecated iOS 26, maintenance mode). If you want a 1-day throwaway prototype, SCNView with allowsCameraControl, SCNGeometry from buffers with a .color source and hitTest(...).faceIndex is the fastest path, but throw it away.

Keep a custom Metal (MTKView) renderer as the escape hatch, not the first implementation: the LowLevelMesh vertex layout above is a plain Metal vertex buffer, so if CustomMaterial or entity overhead disappoints at 1M triangles on the A15 you can move the same chunk buffers to an MTKView renderer (setTriangleFillMode(.lines) for wireframe, id-buffer or CPU BVH for picking) without changing the data model or exporters.

First CI build should be a spike that compiles and logs: ARView(.nonAR) + PerspectiveCamera; one LowLevelMesh chunk with .color attribute; UnlitMaterial with triangleFillMode .lines; a CustomMaterial whose .metal shader emits geometry().color(); generateStaticMesh(from:) + raycast printing triangleHit?.faceIndex; and pixelCast. These are the six facts a wrong guess would cost a CI round trip on, and all six are iOS 18 APIs verified against Apple's doc JSON.
open_questions: Does params.geometry().color() in a CustomMaterial surface shader return the LowLevelMesh .color (uchar4Normalized_bgra) attribute on iOS 18? Strongly implied (VertexSemantic.color exists for this; visionOS shader-graph 'Geometry Color' reads it) but no compiled iOS sample was found. Verify in the first build; fallback: pack colour into uv1/uv0 or use per-face material parts.

Measured RealityKit frame rate on iPhone 13 Pro Max with ~1M triangles in ~200-400 LowLevelMesh entities using CustomMaterial vs UnlitMaterial: no public benchmark exists; needs an on-device test (Apple: 'measure and iterate').

Exact triangleHit.faceIndex semantics when a CollisionComponent holds several ShapeResources (index relative to shapeIndex) and whether faceIndex matches the source triangle order of generateStaticMesh(from: MeshResource) (expected yes; verify by picking a known triangle).
pixelCast(from:to:) cost and whether primitive indexes triangles in original index order for a LowLevelMesh with multiple parts (meshPart id mapping is undocumented).

Whether MeshResource.generate(from: [MeshDescriptor]) is still present in the iOS 26 SDK headers (the doc JSON only lists the Contents overload; community code uses the descriptor overload everywhere). Only matters if you use MeshDescriptor instead of LowLevelMesh.
Whether iOS 26's reworked RealityKit renderer changes CustomMaterial or triangleFillMode behaviour on the second (iOS 26) phone; nothing in the docs indicates deprecation of either.

RealityView on iOS: whether Apple will add combined camera controls or project/unproject; until then ARView remains the practical host, and there is no Apple statement deprecating ARView (forum 788284 has no Apple reply).

verdicts.correction:
Partially wrong. The parts that hold: CustomMaterial, CustomMaterial.SurfaceShader, CustomMaterial.LightingModel (lit/clearcoat/unlit), CustomMaterial.Custom, init(surfaceShader:geometryModifier:lightingModel:) and init(from:surfaceShader:geometryModifier:) are all iOS 15.0+ / macOS 12.0+ and are NOT listed for visionOS (doc JSON platforms omit visionOS). MeshDescriptor.Materials with .allFaces(UInt32) / .perFace([UInt32]) is iOS 15.0+. MeshBuffers has no color semantic (type properties are positions, normals, tangents, bitangents, textureCoordinates, uv2-uv7, jointInfluences, triangleIndices, blendShapeOffsets(named:), plus custom(_:type:)). LowLevelMesh.VertexSemantic.color and LowLevelMesh.Part(materialIndex:) are iOS 18.0+. The Metal-RealityKit-APIs PDF confirms surface side `float4 color() const thread` "Returns the fragment's interpolated vertex color", geometry-modifier side `float4 color()` / `void set_color(float4 value)`, the lighting-model table (.unlit: only set_emissive_color()), and that set_base_color is ignored under .unlit. Apple's own LowLevelMesh doc sample pairs a .color attribute with UnlitMaterial(), and the forum thread (Apple engineer reply) confirms that renders white: built-in materials ignore vertex color.

The wrong part: "ShaderGraphMaterial is visionOS-only". Apple doc JSON lists `struct ShaderGraphMaterial` as iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 26.0+, visionOS 1.0+. `init(materialXLabel: String, data: Data) async throws` (loads from raw MaterialX data, no Reality Composer Pro bundle required) and `init(named:from:in:)` are iOS 18.0+. The shader graph nodes "Geometry Color" (abstract: "The color associated with the geometry at the currently-processed geometric position, typically defined by vertex color") and "Unlit Surface (RealityKit)" / "PBR Surface (RealityKit)" are documented iOS 17.0+ / macOS 14.0+. In forum thread 759449 an Apple engineer states the missing link for LowLevelMesh .color is a ShaderGraphMaterial with Geometry Color -> Unlit Surface. So on the iOS 18 deployment target there are TWO viable per-vertex-color paths: (a) CustomMaterial + Metal surface shader reading params.geometry().color() (iOS 15+, unavailable on visionOS), and (b) ShaderGraphMaterial built from a MaterialX document (geomcolor -> realitykit_unlit surface) via init(materialXLabel:data:) (iOS 18+, also works on visionOS). "Vertex-color display therefore needs CustomMaterial" is false; CustomMaterial is one option, and (b) avoids shipping a .metal file. Caveat for both: neither path has been seen rendering a LowLevelMesh .color attribute in an iOS-compiled sample in this session (the forum confirmation is visionOS; the Metal PDF is dated July 2021, pre-LowLevelMesh); keep the CI verification step and the uv-packing / per-face fallback.

Minor signature nit: the doc declaration is `init(surfaceShader: CustomMaterial.SurfaceShader, geometryModifier: CustomMaterial.GeometryModifier? = nil, lightingModel: CustomMaterial.LightingModel) throws` with NO default for lightingModel (the claim shows `= .lit`); pass it explicitly.

verdicts.claim: No built-in RealityKit material on iOS reads per-vertex colors (MeshDescriptor/MeshBuffers has no color semantic; UnlitMaterial/PBR ignore the LowLevelMesh .color attribute; ShaderGraphMaterial is visionOS-only).
